probe_result: A precommitted proposal deadline plus post-deadline enumeration is not a causal predecessor fence. A writer can pass admission before the boundary, stall before durable proposal, and commit a conflicting payload after the closer has authorized from an incomplete snapshot. Claimed timestamps are insufficient without non-forgeable transport enforcement.
mechanism_revision: Replace temporal closure with causal closure. Either use a genuine admission fence, or avoid an open proposal set by having the predecessor immutably precommit one successor effect_id/payload_hash so all later materializers are identical or fail closed.
scope_guard: Negative evidence is limited to one predecessor, two writers, one locally checked deadline, immutable role-local proposal files, post-boundary enumeration, and one authorization point. Trusted server-enforced cutoffs, fencing tokens, linearizable CAS, closed membership with payload precommit, and equivalent primitives remain outside tested scope.

mechanism_assessment.accepted_scope: counterexample to deadline-only predecessor closure in the finite symbolic model
mechanism_assessment.unresolved_child: Test deterministic single-owner successor precommit as a Chat-native replacement for open proposal admission.

conflict_check: Semantic inputs were limited to frozen sanitized controls and own neuroscience LATEST/preflight/evidence. No O, other-worker, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, other-role receipt/config, scheduler, protected-primary, hosted-compute, paid, finite-credit, or manual-user execution semantics were used.
exact_next_action: Next valid invocation: checkpoint first, then test exactly one deterministic single-owner successor-precommit protocol. Let predecessor e3 immutably choose effect_id and payload_hash before any successor materialization. Stress (1) crash before materialization, (2) duplicate materializers after restart, and (3) a stale invocation attempting a different payload under the same predecessor.
